display.purpose: Hero accuracy metric on Summary screen. At most one per screen.

title.purpose: Section titles, button labels, kanji meanings and readings.

label.purpose: Micro-labels over grouped controls, uppercase with tracking.

shadows.name: lifted-toast
shadows.purpose: Soft, sumi-tinted ambient shadow for floating overlays lifted off the desk.

motion.name: ease-stationery
motion.purpose: Direct, calm transitions without bounce or overshoot.

motion.name: duration-fast

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary affirmative action button (Correct, Start writing).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #c67139; color: #f5ead8; font-family: 'Noto Serif JP', serif; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; min-height: 88px; padding: 16px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease, transform 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #8c491a; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); background: #8c491a; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Secondary drill action (Reveal, Missed) with transparent fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #201e1d; font-family: 'Noto Serif JP', serif; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; min-height: 88px; padding: 16px 24px; border: 1px solid rgba(32, 30, 29, 0.16); border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease, transform 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(32, 30, 29, 0.04); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.98); background: rgba(32, 30, 29, 0.08); }

components.name: Positive Chip
components.description: Read-only affirmative status badge (Stylus found, Session complete).
components.css: .ds-chip-positive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #e1eecc; color: #3d472b; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 10px; }

components.name: Missed Chip
components.description: Attention-framing miss count chip for shaky cards.
components.css: .ds-chip-missed { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #ffe1d0; color: #643312; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 10px; }

components.name: Genkouyoushi Cell
components.description: The pristine writing sheet canvas cell with dashed cross guides.
components.css: .ds-cell { position: relative; width: 180px; height: 180px; background: #f9f4ed; border: 1px solid rgba(32, 30, 29, 0.1); border-radius: 14px; box-sizing: border-box; overflow: hidden; } .ds-cell-guide-h { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 0; right: 0; border-top: 1px dashed #ccdbb2; } .ds-cell-guide-v { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 0; bottom: 0; border-left: 1px dashed #ccdbb2; } .ds-cell-dot { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 4px; height: 4px; margin: -2px 0 0 -2px; background: #ccdbb2; border-radius: 50%; }

components.name: Segmented Pill Group
components.description: Segmented track for single-choice and multi-choice scopes.
components.css: .ds-pill-group { display: inline-flex; background: #ebddc5; padding: 4px; border-radius: 12px; gap: 4px; } .ds-pill { background: transparent; border: none; color: #201e1d; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-pill-active { background: #c67139; color: #f5ead8; }

components.name: Grade Toast
components.description: Floating feedback banner with undo action.
components.html: き · hiragana — missed 3 times
components.css: .ds-toast { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; background: #ffe1d0; color: #643312; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; padding: 14px 20px; border-radius: 18px; box-shadow: 0 12px 32px rgba(32, 30, 29, 0.12); } .ds-toast-undo { background: transparent; border: none; color: #8c491a; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; text-decoration: underline; padding: 0; }

narrative.overview:
tegakko is designed as an unhurried, tactile morning stationery ritual rather than an engagement product. It opens like a fine physical notebook: a prompt, a blank genkouyoushi cell, and warm sumi brush ink. The interface is grounded in the material sensibility of Japanese washi paper, natural mineral pigments, and calligraphy craftsmanship. Every element feels deliberate, permanent, and quiet.

The system rejects the hyperactivity of modern language software. There are no cartoon mascots, no celebratory confetti, no guilt-tripping streak counters, and no loud gamification gimmicks. Instead, the design fosters quiet confidence and honest self-appraisal: errors are not punished with red alerts, and successes are met with calm acknowledgment rather than patronizing praise.
keyCharacteristics: Tactile Paper Surfaces: Warm cream washi grounds the entire viewport; there is no harsh digital white or synthetic gray.
Physical Restraint: Controls behave with physical weight and subtle debossed press feedback rather than bouncy micro-animations.
Single Chromatic Accent: Earthy Japanese Persimmon (kaki) used with extreme discipline, behaving like an artist's personal seal.
Sacred Brushwork: Brushed calligraphy typography (Yuji Syuku) is reserved strictly for genuine Japanese graphemes.

rules.name: The Persimmon Rarity Rule
rules.body: Japanese Persimmon (#c67139) must occupy ≤5% of any rendered viewport. Its visual power stems entirely from rarity. It is never applied to large surface fills, headers, or decorative borders.

rules.name: The No-Red Rule
rules.body: True red (#ff0000 or saturated crimson) is banned from the product. Missed characters and destructive warnings use Soft Peach (#ffe1d0) with rich brown text (#643312) to communicate attention and reflection rather than alarm or failure.

rules.name: The Sacred Brush Rule
rules.body: Yuji Syuku is reserved strictly for genuine Japanese graphemes (kana and kanji reference glyphs). It must never be applied to romaji prompts, English definitions, UI labels, or button text.

rules.name: The Structural Voice Rule
rules.body: All numbers, grades, and structural headers speak in Noto Serif JP 600. Explanatory sentences and instructional captions speak in Figtree 400.

rules.name: The Paper Plane Rule
rules.body: Screens and cards represent the paper itself. They sit flush at rest without elevation shadows or border bevels. Depth is conveyed through tonal layering.

rules.name: The Mechanical Press Rule
rules.body: Buttons and interactive tiles do not elevate on hover. Upon press (:active), they exhibit tactile mechanical debossing: a slight downward scale (transform: scale(0.98)) and tonal deepening.

dos: Do lock screens firmly to 100dvh in portrait orientation (~800×1280px).
Do preserve the Warm Cream Washi ground (#f5ead8) across every screen.
Do pair every status color chip with descriptive text; never communicate state by color alone.
Do maintain a minimum 88px button height for drill grading actions to prevent mis-taps with a stylus.
Do reserve Yuji Syuku tilted at -1.2deg solely for authentic Japanese graphemes.
Do allow Undo on grading only while the grade toast is active or on the frozen final card.
donts: Don't use saturated red (#ff0000, #e53e3e) anywhere in the application.
Don't use pure digital black (#000000) or cold digital grays; always use Deep Sumi Ink (#201e1d).
Don't introduce gamification tropes: no streak fire icons, XP points, confetti animations, or push nudges.
Don't overlay reference stroke templates inside the active genkouyoushi cell; recall must remain unguided.
Don't apply full-pill border radius (9999px) to action buttons or content cards.
Don't add audio sound effects, celebratory chimes, or buzzer sounds on grading.
